                   400.0 019FA031-620C-7FA7-BD70-37112AA74883 NULL                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             The Strix Harvest Frame ran warm through his chest. It was woven filament and a lattice that drank in every step and every breath and banked it as charge. At rest he could feel it against his sternum, a low, constant heat.

Other men forgot the watch on their wrist. He never forgot the frame. It was the one thing on him that was always on.

Later — in a lobby two floors up, at a hearing that hadn't happened yet — Brandt would straighten. A small motion, just the weight resettling, the shoulders pulling back an inch. The colonel's posture. The institutional reflex. Bear would not move his right hand. He would nod once. That was all. The absence of a returned gesture — that was the thing that would matter.
